claim: Erhvervsakademi SydVest is the former name of the current SEA; the legacy Business Academy SouthWest lead reuses dk-sea.
excerpt: The alumni page identifies Erhvervsakademi Sydvest as now named SEA - Syddansk Erhvervsakademi. Footer locations: Esbjerg, Sønderborg and Tønder; CVR 31689791.

publisher: Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science
claim: The Danish Agency lists EA Business Academy SouthWest among its recognised business academies; SEA supplies its current name.
excerpt: Structured restatement: the Agency names EA Business Academy SouthWest, links easv.dk, and describes business academies as independent institutions regulated by the academies act.

claim: SEA lists two English first-year AP programmes in Esbjerg; the other two English degrees require prior AP study.
excerpt: Structured restatement: Computer Science and Multimedia Design are AP degrees in Esbjerg starting in August. Software Development and Web Development are bachelor top-ups; their programme pages require prior AP study. Student Services offers study counselling, IT, SU, internship and study-abroad guidance.
interpretation: Top-up admission requirements were also read at https://www.s-e-a.dk/uddannelser/software-development and https://www.s-e-a.dk/uddannelser/web-development. They do not create first-year Opportunities.

claim: SEA publishes the AP curriculum, separate subject and English-proof requirements, and quota 1/quota 2 selection.
excerpt: Structured restatement: English-taught Esbjerg AP; 2.5 years, five semesters, programming/system development and fifth-semester internship; Mathematics B and English B. Quota 1 ranks on converted GPA and is described for EU/EEA citizens; quota 2 uses other documented qualifications and a motivation letter. English tests are required for foreign exams unless exempt; the listed International Baccalaureate exam exemption does not explicitly mention Course Results. The 5 July 2027 headline concerns quota 1; international applications use 15 March at noon.
interpretation: The full IB Diploma exemption is retained from the existing accepted record. Course Results exemption is unresolved. English B remains a separate subject requirement. Programme-page factor weights and historical cut-offs are not published; no number is inferred. Current test list: IELTS 6.5; TOEFL internet 94 or paper 560; Cambridge Proficiency/Advanced; Oxford Placement B2 (75 in each part); CEFR B2/C1; tests under two years old. The national promotion catalogue still quotes TOEFL 83, which does not override SEA.

claim: SEA publishes AP application documents, fee exemptions and group-specific document guidance; final IB timing needs an agreed arrangement.
excerpt: Structured restatement: optagelse.dk applications with an international qualification close 15 March at noon. Current transcripts may precede graduation. The EU section allows enclosures until 5 July noon, non-EU until 1 May noon, and later diplomas require contacting SEA. The date table retains a 26 August 2026 start. EU/EEA/Swiss students and listed qualifying residence-permit holders are tuition-exempt; others pay.
interpretation: No 2027 document deadline is confirmed: the FAQ gives 1 April for international qualifying examinations. No separate predicted-grade deadline or automatic late-final-IB permission is published. Contact arrangement is an open action, not a rejection.

claim: SEA FAQ gives an international-exam document date conflicting with its full-degree guide and limits housing assistance to exchange students.
excerpt: Structured restatement: summer documents generally reach 5 July but applicants with international qualifying examinations are given 1 April. NemStudie carries messages, offers and acceptance. Housing help is limited to Erasmus/exchange students. The important-dates table retains a 2026 study start.
interpretation: Keep the FAQ and EU/non-EU guide disagreement visible rather than silently selecting a date. No disputed date was added as an actionable 2027 milestone.

claim: SEA links a tariff labelled 2024/2027; autumn 2027 applicability is unconfirmed.
excerpt: Structured restatement of the visually read AP table: semester one including registration EUR 7,500 / DKK 56,250; semester two EUR 4,900 / DKK 36,750; year two (semesters three and four) EUR 8,000 / DKK 60,000; Computer Science semester five EUR 2,000 / DKK 15,000. The heading reads 2024/2027. Retaking year one is a separate EUR 8,000 / DKK 60,000 charge.
interpretation: No programme total or annual average is asserted, no double counting of semester three/four, no registration amount invented, and no autumn 2027 price confirmation. PDF was rendered to PNG and its table visually inspected.
